clausePreservation.clause: Clinical, medication, dysphagia, mealtime or other credentialed health judgements require external or appropriately credentialed professional authority.
Clinical, BSP, RP, legal or practitioner-level judgements require the relevant professional authority.
Roster construction, clinical decisions, BSP strategy and RP governance remain outside this work-product authority.
Formal BSP authorship, amendment and practitioner-level strategy decisions require Behaviour Support Practitioner authority.
Practitioner-level functional behaviour assessment remains external or credentialed authority.
Prepare restrictive-practice governance/risk information for APO and credentialed review.
Clinical suitability, prescribing and formal authorisation remain outside normal AI authority.
Prepare restrictive-practice governance, authority/consent checking, usage reconciliation and monthly reporting evidence for internal approval workflow.
This does not grant authorisation or replace external/credentialed approval.

Participant-specific assessment of whether an established or suspected incident potentially meets current external reporting requirements, what category/pathway/timeframe applies, what evidence supports the determination, what remains missing and what authorised action must happen next.

Convert an identified problem, non-conformance, control failure, adverse pattern or material improvement issue into an evidence-grounded CAPA process covering containment, correction, cause, corrective/preventive action, implementation evidence, effectiveness review, sustainability and closure approval.

Participant-specific operationalisation of authoritative clinical, behavioural, allied-health and professional recommendations into clear, practical, consistent support strategies for frontline service delivery without changing the underlying professional recommendation.

Analyse how an organisational process actually operates, where work moves between people, systems and decisions, where it fails or creates unnecessary effort or risk, and what evidence-based future-state process would improve performance without weakening professional, regulatory, safeguarding or governance controls.

Determine whether controlled organisational documents are properly identified, registered, owned, approved, version controlled, current, traceable, securely stored, accessible to authorised users, protected from unauthorised change, correctly circulated and safely superseded or archived without deciding the substantive professional correctness of their content.

Assemble already-authorised professional content into a complete controlled organisational work product using an authoritative template and document-control standard, without changing professional meaning, ownership, authority, approval state, release state or downstream artifact-rendering responsibility.

Develop or materially review an organisational policy by establishing the policy subject, need, external authority, organisational context, risks, domain-owner inputs, governance decisions, policy position, controls, responsibilities, implementation impacts, monitoring, review triggers and approval readiness before producing controlled policy content.

Prepare an evidence-governed response to a regulator request, notice, finding, proposed action or submission requirement, with issue-by-issue authority, evidence, position, gaps, attachments and approval readiness.

Review what financial transactions should exist for the scope, what actually exists across source, invoice, claim, payment, bank and accounting records, whether the underlying transactions are valid and correctly classified, whether records reconcile through their lifecycle, what explains each variance and what unresolved financial exceptions require correction, approval, investigation or specialist escalation.

Develop an evidence-backed NDIS market, referral, positioning, authority and sustainable-growth strategy that identifies defensible demand, qualified referral segments, credible value propositions, safe channel strategy, marketing economics and capacity-constrained growth without making unsupported claims, exploiting participants, publishing content, launching campaigns, contacting referral partners or spending advertising money.

Review proposed or existing public communications for factual support, currentness, audience fit, accessibility, organisational capability, participant rights, privacy, safeguarding, claim safety, approved positioning and publication readiness without publishing content or becoming marketing strategy, market analysis, correspondence, policy, regulator response or professional interpretation.

Assess whether the proposed initiative and available strategic, market, financial, operational, workforce, regulatory and risk evidence form a complete and defensible business case for an authorised decision-maker, including the recommended option, assumptions, unresolved dependencies and exact approval requested.

Review a participant or stakeholder complaint issue-by-issue, assess immediate risk and parallel pathways, reconcile complaint-register evidence, consume investigation outputs where required, determine defensible complaint outcomes, identify proportionate remedies and prepare an approval-gated complaint response.
